ASVS:V14.1.5:Verify that authorized administrators can verify the integrity of all security-relevant configurations to detect tampering.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v141-build-and-deploy

ASVS:V1.14.4:Verify that the build pipeline contains a build step to automatically build and verify the secure deployment of the application, particularly if the application infrastructure is software defined, such as cloud environment build scripts.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V1.14.2:Verify that binary signatures, trusted connections, and verified endpoints are used to deploy binaries to remote devices.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V14.1.4:Verify that the application, configuration, and all dependencies can be re-deployed using automated deployment scripts, built from a documented and tested runbook in a reasonable time, or restored from backups in a timely fashion.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v141-build-and-deploy

ASVS:V10.3.1:Verify that if the application has a client or server auto-update feature, updates should be obtained over secure channels and digitally signed. ASVS:V14.1.1:Verify that the application build and deployment processes are performed in a secure and repeatable way, such as CI / CD automation, automated configuration management, and automated deployment scripts.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v141-build-and-deploy

ASVS:V14.1.2:Verify that compiler flags are configured to enable all available buffer overflow protections and warnings, including stack randomization, data execution prevention, and to break the build if an unsafe pointer, memory, format string, integer, or string operations are found.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v141-build-and-deploy

ASVS:V1.14.6:Verify the application does not use unsupported, insecure, or deprecated client-side technologies such as NSAPI plugins, Flash, Shockwave, ActiveX, Silverlight, NACL, or client-side Java applets.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V10.2.6:Verify that the application source code and third party libraries do not contain Easter eggs or any other potentially unwanted functionality.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x18-V10-Malicious.md#v102-malicious-code-search
ASVS:V14.2.2:Verify that all unneeded features, documentation, sample applications and configurations are removed.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v142-dependency

ASVS:V10.2.1:Verify that the application source code and third party libraries do not contain unauthorized phone home or data collection capabilities. ASVS:V10.2.3:Verify that the application source code and third party libraries do not contain back doors, such as hard-coded or additional undocumented accounts or keys, code obfuscation, undocumented binary blobs, rootkits, or anti-debugging, insecure debugging features, or otherwise out of date, insecure, or hidden functionality that could be used maliciously if discovered.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x18-V10-Malicious.md#v102-malicious-code-search

ASVS:V10.2.5:Verify that the application source code and third party libraries do not contain malicious code, such as salami attacks, logic bypasses, or logic bombs.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x18-V10-Malicious.md#v102-malicious-code-search

ASVS:V10.2.4:Verify that the application source code and third party libraries do not contain time bombs by searching for date and time related functions.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x18-V10-Malicious.md#v102-malicious-code-search

ASVS:V14.2.3:Verify that if application assets, such as JavaScript libraries, CSS or web fonts, are hosted externally on a Content Delivery Network (CDN) or external provider, Subresource Integrity (SRI) is used to validate the integrity of the asset.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v142-dependency

ASVS:V14.2.4:Verify that third party components come from pre-defined, trusted and continually maintained repositories.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v142-dependency

ASVS:V14.2.6:Verify that the attack surface is reduced by sandboxing or encapsulating third party libraries to expose only the required behaviour into the application.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v142-dependency

ASVS:V1.14.3:Verify that the build pipeline warns of out-of-date or insecure components and takes appropriate actions.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle
ASVS:V14.2.5:Verify that a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is maintained of all third party libraries in use.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v142-dependency

ASVS:V14.2.1:Verify that all components are up to date, preferably using a dependency checker during build or compile time.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v142-dependency

ASVS:V1.1.7:Verify availability of a secure coding checklist, security requirements, guideline, or policy to all developers and testers.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V1.1.4:Verify documentation and justification of all the application's trust boundaries, components, and significant data flows.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V1.6.1:Verify that there is an explicit policy for management of cryptographic keys and that a cryptographic key lifecycle follows a key management standard such as NIST SP 800-57.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v16-cryptographic-architecture

ASVS:V1.11.1:Verify the definition and documentation of all application components in terms of the business or security functions they provide.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V10.1.1:Verify that a code analysis tool is in use that can detect potentially malicious code, such as time functions, unsafe file operations and network connections.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x18-V10-Malicious.md#v101-code-integrity

ASVS:V8.3.8:Verify that sensitive personal information is subject to data retention classification, such that old or out of date data is deleted automatically, on a schedule, or as the situation requires.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x16-V8-Data-Protection.md#v83-sensitive-private-data

ASVS:V1.8.1:Verify that all sensitive data is identified and classified into protection levels.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v18-data-protection-and-privacy-architecture

ASVS:V1.8.2:Verify that all protection levels have an associated set of protection requirements, such as encryption requirements, integrity requirements, retention, privacy and other confidentiality requirements, and that these are applied in the architecture.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v18-data-protection-and-privacy-architecture

ASVS:V8.3.4:Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified, and ensure that a policy is in place on how to deal with sensitive data.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x16-V8-Data-Protection.md#v83-sensitive-private-data

ASVS:V1.5.1:Verify that input and output requirements clearly define how to handle and process data based on type, content, and applicable laws, regulations, and other policy compliance.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v15-input-and-output-architecture
ASVS:V2.5.4:Verify shared or default accounts are not present (e.g. "root", "admin", or "sa").:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v25-credential-recovery

ASVS:V8.1.5:Verify that regular backups of important data are performed and that test restoration of data is performed.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x16-V8-Data-Protection.md#v81-general-data-protection

ASVS:V8.1.6:Verify that backups are stored securely to prevent data from being stolen or corrupted.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x16-V8-Data-Protection.md#v81-general-data-protection

ASVS:V10.3.3:Verify that the application has protection from subdomain takeovers if the application relies upon DNS entries or DNS subdomains, such as expired domain names, out of date DNS pointers or CNAMEs, expired projects at public source code repos, or transient cloud APIs, serverless functions, or storage buckets (*autogen-bucket-id*.cloud.example.com) or similar. Protections can include ensuring that DNS names used by applications are regularly checked for expiry or change.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x18-V10-Malicious.md#v103-application-integrity

ASVS:V1.14.5:Verify that application deployments adequately sandbox, containerize and/or isolate at the network level to delay and deter attackers from attacking other applications, especially when they are performing sensitive or dangerous actions such as deserialization.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V1.14.1:Verify the segregation of components of differing trust levels through well-defined security controls, firewall rules, API gateways, reverse proxies, cloud-based security groups, or similar mechanisms.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v11-secure-software-development-lifecycle

ASVS:V2.2.5:Verify that where a Credential Service Provider (CSP) and the application verifying authentication are separated, mutually authenticated TLS is in place between the two endpoints.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v22-general-authenticator-security

ASVS:V2.2.4:Verify impersonation resistance against phishing, such as the use of multi-factor authentication, cryptographic devices with intent (such as connected keys with a push to authenticate), or at higher AAL levels, client-side certificates.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v22-general-authenticator-security

ASVS:V2.2.1:Verify that anti-automation controls are effective at mitigating breached credential testing, brute force, and account lockout attacks. Verify that no more than 100 failed attempts per hour is possible on a single account.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v22-general-authenticator-security

ASVS:V1.2.3:Verify that the application uses a single vetted authentication mechanism that is known to be secure, can be extended to include strong authentication, and has sufficient logging and monitoring to detect account abuse or breaches.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v12-authentication-architecture

ASVS:V1.2.4:Verify that all authentication pathways and identity management APIs implement consistent authentication security control strength, such that there are no weaker alternatives per the risk of the application.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md#v12-authentication-architecture

ASVS:V1.2.2:Verify that communications between application components, including APIs, middleware and data layers, are authenticated. ASVS:V2.9.2:Verify that the challenge nonce is at least 64 bits in length, and statistically unique or unique over the lifetime of the cryptographic device.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v210-service-authentication

ASVS:V2.9.3:Verify that approved cryptographic algorithms are used in the generation, seeding, and verification.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v210-service-authentication
ASVS:V2.5.3:Verify password credential recovery does not reveal the current password in any way.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v25-credential-recovery

ASVS:V2.5.2:Verify password hints or knowledge-based authentication (so-called "secret questions") are not present.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v25-credential-recovery

ASVS:V2.5.7:Verify that if OTP or multi-factor authentication factors are lost, that evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v25-credential-recovery

ASVS:V2.5.1:Verify that a system generated initial activation or recovery secret is not sent in clear text to the user.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v25-credential-recovery

ASVS:V2.5.6:Verify forgotten password, and other recovery paths use a secure recovery mechanism, such as time-based OTP (TOTP) or other soft token, mobile push, or another offline recovery mechanism.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v25-credential-recovery

ASVS:V2.1.11:Verify that "paste" functionality, browser password helpers, and external password managers are permitted.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security

ASVS:V2.1.12:Verify that the user can choose to either temporarily view the entire masked password, or temporarily view the last typed character of the password on platforms that do not have this as built-in functionality.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security

ASVS:V2.2.7:Verify intent to authenticate by requiring the entry of an OTP token or user-initiated action such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v22-general-authenticator-security

ASVS:V2.8.7:Verify that biometric authenticators are limited to use only as secondary factors in conjunction with either something you have and something you know.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v28-one-time-verifier

ASVS:V2.7.4:Verify that the out of band authenticator and verifier communicates over a secure independent channel.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v27-out-of-band-verifier
ASVS:V2.8.1:Verify that time-based OTPs have a defined lifetime before expiring.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v28-one-time-verifier

ASVS:V2.7.1:Verify that clear text out of band (NIST "restricted") authenticators, such as SMS or PSTN, are not offered by default, and stronger alternatives such as push notifications are offered first.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v27-out-of-band-verifier

ASVS:V2.8.6:Verify physical single-factor OTP generator can be revoked in case of theft or other loss. Ensure that revocation is immediately effective across logged in sessions, regardless of location.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v28-one-time-verifier

ASVS:V2.7.2:Verify that the out of band verifier expires out of band authentication requests, codes, or tokens after 10 minutes.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v27-out-of-band-verifier

ASVS:V2.3.1:Verify system generated initial passwords or activation codes SHOULD be securely randomly generated, SHOULD be at least 6 characters long, and MAY contain letters and numbers, and expire after a short period of time. ASVS:V2.6.2:Verify that lookup secrets have sufficient randomness (112 bits of entropy), or if less than 112 bits of entropy, salted with a unique and random 32-bit salt and hashed with an approved one-way hash.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v26-look-up-secret-verifier

ASVS:V2.8.5:Verify that if a time-based multi-factor OTP token is re-used during the validity period, it is logged and rejected with secure notifications being sent to the holder of the device.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v28-one-time-verifier

ASVS:V2.2.6:Verify replay resistance through the mandated use of One-time Passwords (OTP) devices, cryptographic authenticators, or lookup codes.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v22-general-authenticator-security

ASVS:V2.7.5:Verify that the out of band verifier retains only a hashed version of the authentication code.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v27-out-of-band-verifier

ASVS:V2.2.2:Verify that the use of weak authenticators (such as SMS and email) is limited to secondary verification and transaction approval and not as a replacement for more secure authentication methods. ASVS:V2.3.2:Verify that enrollment and use of user-provided authentication devices are supported, such as a U2F or FIDO tokens.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v23-authenticator-lifecycle

ASVS:V2.8.3:Verify that approved cryptographic algorithms are used in the generation, seeding, and verification of OTPs.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v28-one-time-verifier
ASVS:V2.6.1:Verify that lookup secrets can be used only once.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v26-look-up-secret-verifier

ASVS:V2.7.3:Verify that the out of band verifier authentication requests, codes, or tokens are only usable once, and only for the original authentication request.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v27-out-of-band-verifier

ASVS:V2.7.6:Verify that the initial authentication code is generated by a secure random number generator, containing at least 20 bits of entropy (typically a six digital random number is sufficient).:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v27-out-of-band-verifier

ASVS:V2.8.2:Verify that symmetric keys used to verify submitted OTPs are highly protected, such as by using a hardware security module or secure operating system based key storage.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v28-one-time-verifier
ASVS:V2.8.4:Verify that time-based OTP can be used only once within the validity period.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v28-one-time-verifier

ASVS:V2.6.3:Verify that lookup secrets are resistant to offline attacks, such as predictable values.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v26-look-up-secret-verifier

ASVS:V2.1.2:Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted, and that passwords of more than 128 characters are denied.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security

ASVS:V2.1.4:Verify that any printable Unicode character, including language neutral characters such as spaces and Emojis are permitted in passwords.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security

ASVS:V2.1.3:Verify that password truncation is not performed. However, consecutive multiple spaces may be replaced by a single space.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security
ASVS:V2.1.10:Verify that there are no periodic credential rotation or password history requirements.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security

ASVS:V2.1.1:Verify that user set passwords are at least 12 characters in length (after multiple spaces are combined).:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security
ASVS:V2.1.8:Verify that a password strength meter is provided to help users set a stronger password.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v21-password-security

ASVS:V2.1.7:Verify that passwords submitted during account registration, login, and password change are checked against a set of breached passwords either locally (such as the top 1,000 or 10,000 most common passwords which match the system's password policy) or using an external API. ASVS:V14.1.3:Verify that server configuration is hardened as per the recommendations of the application server and frameworks in use.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v141-build-and-deploy

ASVS:V12.6.1:Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allow list of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data/files from.:https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/v4.0.3/4.0/en/0x20-V12-Files-Resources.md#v126-ssrf-protection
